title: QwenLM/qwen-code — An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.
content:
The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat.
中文 | Deutsch | français | 日本語 | Русский | Português (Brasil) | 한국어
- Agentic out of the box — Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP. Dynamic workflows, zero setup.
- Open-source, inside and out — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in.
- Multi-protocol — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime.
- Beyond the terminal — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / Feishu).
Tip
Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI.
Linux / macOS:
curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash
Windows:
irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex
Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.
NPM / Homebrew
NPM (requires Node.js 22+):
npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest
Homebrew (macOS / Linux):
brew install qwen-code
Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code:
cd /path/to/your-project
qwen
Inside the session, run /auth to configure your provider and API key. Then try:
Explain this repository and show me where to start.
See the Authentication Guide and Settings Reference for detailed setup.
Choose the interface that fits your workflow:
For automation and custom integrations:
- Headless — Run qwen -p "..." in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs.
- SDKs — Build with TypeScript, Python, or Java.
- Daemon — Run qwen serve to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). (experimental) Daemon guide.
- Computer Use — Set up native MCP tools or Node REPL + SDK in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python)
import asyncio
from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query
async def main() -> None:
    result = query(
        "Summarize the repository layout.",
        {
            "cwd": "/path/to/project",
            "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen",
        },
    )
    async for message in result:
        if is_sdk_result_message(message):
            print(message["result"])
asyncio.run(main())
Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions.
Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell:
qwen serve --open
The default address is http://127.0.0.1:4170. To run and manage it in the background instead:
qwen daemon start
qwen daemon status
qwen daemon logs -f
qwen daemon stop
By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN and use --require-auth. See the Daemon guide for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API.
If you know Claude Code, you already know Qwen Code — and then some. We've put significant effort into bringing Qwen Code to feature parity with Claude Code, improving both breadth and reliability across the board.
On SWE-bench Verified, seven Qwen Code versions scored 76.40%–77.80% on average using the same Qwen 3.7 Max model (500 tasks, three trials per version).
Full results and evaluation configuration →
- Qwen Code Desktop — Official desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux
- AionUi — A modern GUI for command-line AI tools including Qwen Code
- Gemini CLI Desktop — A cross-platform desktop/web/mobile UI for Qwen Code
- qwen-audio-agent — Realtime full-duplex voice frontend for Qwen Code over ACP — talk hands-free with barge-in and a local wake word
- 🦞 Qwen Code Claw — Let other agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) delegate coding tasks to Qwen Code via ACP. Paste this prompt into your agent:
Use Qwen Code as a coding agent. First, fetch and read this skill reference:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/refs/heads/main/.qwen/skills/qwen-code-claw/SKILL.md
Then follow the instructions inside to install, authenticate, and use Qwen Code via acpx for all coding tasks.
- Aliyun Model Studio CLI — Official CLI for Aliyun's AI platform (bailian-cli). Extends Qwen Code with image/video generation, knowledge retrieval, app orchestration, and model deployment
See the Terms of Service and Privacy Notice, including Chrome extension and Browser Use data handling.
Contributions are welcome! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.
This project was originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2. We gratefully acknowledge the Gemini CLI team's excellent work. Starting from Qwen Code v0.1, we stopped syncing with upstream and began independent development as a multi-protocol, multi-platform agent framework with deep integrations for Qwen models and beyond.

report.summary: Qwen releases Qwen Code, an open-source terminal AI coding agent with multi-model support that scores up to 77.8% on SWE-bench Verified.
report.background: Terminal-resident coding agents became a major AI category in 2025, led by Anthropic's Claude Code, then Google's open-source Gemini CLI, OpenAI's Codex CLI and a wave of forks. Qwen Code started as a fork of Gemini CLI v0.8.2 but stopped syncing upstream at v0.1 and rebuilt itself as an independent, multi-protocol agent framework. The release reflects the fact that developers increasingly mix models instead of staying with one vendor, and that Alibaba's Qwen team is trying to pair its open-weight models with an equally open tool. It also fits a pattern in which Chinese labs compete for influence in developer tooling, ensuring their models are easy to slot into everyday workflows, while Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio provides a paid, integrated path for teams that want more.
key_points: Qwen Code supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs, along with local models through Ollama or vLLM, and lets you switch at runtime. That is a clear break from tools tied to one provider, and it gives developers a way to swap models in or out as prices and quality shift.

Agent capabilities come as standard. Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams and MCP mean the tool can break work into subtasks, remember project context and plug into external services, all without needing extra setup before the first prompt.

On SWE-bench Verified, seven versions of Qwen Code averaged between 76.40% and 77.80% with the same Qwen 3.7 Max model, across 500 tasks and three trials per version. That puts it close to the top of the class in real-world bug fixing.

It is more than a terminal tool. There are IDE plugins, a desktop app, a Web Shell, TypeScript, Python and Java SDKs, a long-running daemon that serves sessions over HTTP and SSE, headless mode for CI and CD, and chat integrations with Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat and Feishu.

The project uses itself: the team runs its own agent and models to file issues, submit pull requests, review code and run tests. One caution comes with that: the daemon listens on loopback without authentication by default, so any local process can reach the API, including code execution.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this tightens the race over coding agents, which are the most proven commercial use of large models. Qwen Code being open source and model-agnostic puts pressure on closed tools and makes the model layer more of a commodity than the agent layer. For developers, it means a free, hackable alternative to Claude Code with a similar command set, plus SDKs and a daemon that make it easier to automate, self-host and delegate. For regular users, the desktop app, chat bots and voice frontend bring agentic coding to non-terminal users, though the default no-auth daemon, its shell-level code execution and the data handling behind browser features mean teams should review settings before deploying it on shared hosts.
report.tools: Worth trying: Qwen Code itself, which installs via curl, npm or Homebrew; the Qwen Code Desktop app and AionUi for a graphical interface; Gemini CLI Desktop as a cross-platform web UI; qwen-audio-agent for hands-free voice control over ACP; Qwen Code Claw, which lets Claude or Codex delegate tasks to it; and Aliyun Model Studio CLI for image, video and deployment features. Pair these with Ollama or vLLM for local models.
